name: Visto per residenza elettiva (Elective Residency visa)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires stable, continuous passive income of at least approximately EUR 31,000/year (precisely EUR 31,159.29 per the Decreto Interministeriale MAE 850/2011 formula: 3x the Table A subsistence figure) from sources other than employment -- pensions, annuities, real-estate income, stable business holdings, or investment income. Working in Italy is explicitly prohibited on this status. Passive-income requirement rises by 20% for an accompanying spouse and at least 5% per accompanying child, minor or adult dependent.
requirements.fix_path: Document passive income at or above the current threshold, adjusted upward for any accompanying family members.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires availability of housing to establish residence in Italy -- ownership or a rental contract of at least 1 year.
requirements.fix_path: Secure ownership or a qualifying rental contract for Italian accommodation.

evidence_required.document: Documented proof of stable passive income (pension statements, rental income records, dividend/investment statements)
Property deed or rental contract for Italian accommodation
International health insurance, minimum 30 days' duration and EUR 30,000 coverage for emergency hospitalisation and repatriation

outcome.duration_length: 1 year initially, renewable in further periods (commonly cited as up to 2 years per renewal) indefinitely provided the income and other conditions continue to be met

sources.title: Consolato d'Italia Recife (esteri.it, official Italian consular network) -- Visto per residenza elettiva, describing the no-employment condition, housing requirement, and passive-income sources

notes: Distinguished sharply from it_self_employment_visa and it_work_visa_subordinato: this status is explicitly premised on NOT working in Italy at all, the mirror image of Brazil's retirement-visa pattern documented elsewhere in this dataset. work_rights is correctly 'none' rather than 'restricted' -- multiple sources note Italian administrative case law has become notably strict in scrutinising elective-residency applications specifically to confirm the applicant genuinely does not intend to seek local employment, treating any sign of intended work-market participation as grounds for refusal. The EUR 31,000 figure derives from a specific bureaucratic formula (Decreto Interministeriale MAE 850/2011: a daily subsistence rate of EUR 27.89 for days beyond 20, multiplied by 365, plus a fixed EUR 206.58 component, tripled) rather than being a simple round legislative number -- worth flagging since the exact figure (EUR 31,159.29 per source, vs the more commonly rounded EUR 31,000 cited elsewhere) reflects a genuine calculation rather than an approximation, and applicants should expect consulates to apply the precise figure rather than the rounded one. If a denial occurs, appeal lies to the TAR Lazio (Regional Administrative Court) within 60 days -- a specific, centralised judicial-review venue rather than a general administrative appeal, worth noting given how routinely sources describe recent refusals. pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months use the general 5-year/10-year tracks since no accelerated path specific to elective-residency holders was found in sources checked for this build.
